articles.title: Trump Media group stares down $1bn debt crunch as bitcoin bet fades
articles.summary: The Trump family's media group may soon be forced to sell hundreds of millions' worth of assets, including some of its crypto holdings, or take...
articles.body:
The Trump family's media group may soon be forced to sell hundreds of millions' worth of assets, including some of its crypto holdings, or take on costly new borrowing as it comes under pressure to repay up to $1bn in debt.

Trump Media & Technology Group (TMTG), which runs the Truth Social app and is controlled by Donald Trump's family, faces a November 30 deadline to repay convertible bonds it sold last May to fund its creation of a "bitcoin treasury" to hoard digital currency.

But shares in TMTG have plunged and bitcoin has fallen by about a third in the past year, despite the Trump administration ushering in a more permissive era for cryptocurrencies.

The company's waning share price, which is down more than 60 per cent this year to $4.64, has meant lenders to the company who had hoped to convert their notes to stock at $34.72 are deeply out of the money.

Noteholders have therefore been left with little incentive to hold the bonds rather than forcing the company to repay them for cash at face value at the end of the month.

The Trump family media group has placed crypto at the heart of its business, with its former chief executive and chair Devin Nunes calling it a "crucial part of our assets".

Despite President Trump previously calling bitcoin a "scam" in 2021, he has become an ardent supporter of the asset in his second term and pledged to make the US the "crypto capital of the world".

A potential debt redemption of $1bn would further strain the lossmaking media group's finances and could force it to part with some of its cryptocurrency investments, the company's most valuable asset worth around $1.36bn at the end of the third quarter.

TMTG reported a loss of $234mn for the nine months to September.

One investor who is demanding repayment said he expected others would do the same. "Everyone will," he said. "It makes no sense not to."

The looming debt repayment comes at a pivotal moment for the company — whose largest shareholder is President Trump — as it seeks to close a merger with lossmaking nuclear fusion start-up TAE Technologies by the end of the year. TMTG has already lent TAE $300mn.

Although TMTG's interim CEO Kevin McGurn has boasted of its "big balance sheet", many of the company's almost $2.5bn in assets may not be immediately available to generate cash to pay bondholders.

In its most recent quarterly filing, TMTG said it could enter a credit facility to refinance all or a portion of the convertible notes. But it also said such a move could be on unfavourable terms at a high interest rate and may not happen.
authors: George Steer and Antoine Gara and Ramsay Hodgson

articles.title: Hyperliquid's HYPE Token Shows Resilience as Crypto Market Crash Deepens
articles.summary: Hyperliquid's HYPE is outperforming Bitcoin and Ethereum amid the crypto crash. Bitunix analysts explain what's next.
articles.body:
Hyperliquid's HYPE token has lost roughly a quarter of its value since its peak. Yet amid the latest crypto market crash, it is holding up better than Bitcoin and Ethereum. Its derivatives market offers one possible explanation.

HYPE traded near $73 on Friday, down approximately 7% over seven days. Bitcoin lost more than 9% during the same period, while Ethereum dropped nearly 14%.

The token's recent decline followed a rally above $95 in late October, driven partly by excitement over a partnership involving Trade.xyz and Intercontinental Exchange, the New York Stock Exchange's parent company.

Why HYPE Is Holding Up Better Than Bitcoin and Ethereum

According to Bitunix's latest research, HYPE's notional open interest on Hyperliquid declined from $1.21 billion to $1.07 billion, approximately 12%.

Ethereum's open interest on the same platform fell more than 52% over a comparable period.

Open interest measures the value of outstanding futures positions. A smaller decline suggests traders have maintained more exposure to HYPE despite falling prices, although price changes also affect the dollar value of positions.

Bitunix also identified an early HYPE whale holding over $40 million in unrealized profits as of November 12.

Meanwhile, Hyperliquid Strategies reported holding 38.52 million HYPE, approximately 16% of circulating supply, as of September 30.

Why the Broader Crypto Market Keeps Falling

Bitcoin dropped below $70,000 on Friday, reaching approximately $68,700. Ethereum slipped toward $1,930.

Institutional withdrawals remain a concern. US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded another $284.1 million in outflows on November 12, their sixth consecutive negative session.

Data shows approximately $2.8 billion in withdrawals since October 30.

Ethereum ETFs also lost $70.5 million on November 12.

Persistent US inflation has strengthened expectations of further Federal Reserve tightening. Falling prices have also triggered leveraged liquidations, accelerating the downturn.

WhaleRadar data showed $641 million in HYPE shorts against $515 million in longs among tracked large traders on November 13.

$70 remains the immediate level to watch.

Below that, the 200-day moving average near $68.60 offers another potential support area.

A deeper decline could threaten leveraged long positions clustered around $65.50.

A recovery above $74.40, followed by 76–77, would improve the short-term outlook.

HYPE's relative strength is encouraging, but sustained price recovery will depend on fresh buying demand and whether existing support levels survive the broader market downturn.

articles.title: Bitcoin's four-year cycle is about to turn bullish — if history repeats: Chart of the Day
articles.summary: Bitcoin’s slide has hit the window where past bear markets bottomed.
articles.body:
Bitcoin just lost about a sixth of its value in four days, sliding to its lowest level since July. If its four-year cycle holds, the selling is running short on time.

From Wednesday afternoon to its low Saturday night near $62,000, bitcoin ( BTC-USD ) fell about 17%, erasing roughly $250 billion in market value, according to Yahoo Finance calculations. At that low it was down about half from its record. It also slipped below its 200-day moving average , a long-term trend line traders watch closely.

Scott Melker, host of The Daily Wolf, used to think the cycle was dead.

"I was actually a deep believer that the four-year cycle was over," Melker told Yahoo Finance at its Invest conference Thursday.

But bitcoin "topped almost to the day of when any four-year cycle predictor would have [pointed to]," he said, and the yearlong slide since then "really does align."

The clock is based on the halving , which cuts the reward for mining new bitcoin in half about every four years and slows the coin's supply growth. The last four came in 2012, 2016, 2020 and 2024, all presidential election years. Each cycle's record followed 12 to 18 months later.

The peaks have arrived on a near-identical schedule. Bitcoin's October 2025 record came 1,426 days after its November 2021 peak, according to Yahoo Finance calculations using CoinMarketCap data. The two peaks before that were 1,424 days apart.

The last three bear markets bottomed 12 to 13 months after the peak, the same pattern that showed up when the Binance hack knocked $100 billion off crypto . Bitcoin just passed 13 months since its Oct. 6, 2025 record.

This cycle has already gone off script once.

Bitcoin's lowest price so far came July 1, near $57,750. That was just nine months after the peak, and 54% below the record. Past bear markets cut far deeper, by 77% to 85%. If July was the bottom, this was the shortest and shallowest bitcoin bear market yet.

That leaves two paths. Bitcoin could revisit the early July low, about 7% below Saturday's low, and turn from there. Or July was the bottom, and the latest slide ends at a higher low. Either way, if the cycle holds, the calendar points to a turn in the coming weeks or months.

The midterm elections line up too. Each of the last three bear-market lows came within about 10 weeks after a midterm vote, and this year's was early November. In the year after each of those lows, bitcoin more than doubled.

Still, three cycles is a small sample, and the pattern has broken before. In March 2024, bitcoin set a record ahead of that year's halving, a first.

articles.title: Interest in Trump’s meme coin dinner fades as $TRUMP sinks to record lows
articles.summary: By Michelle Conlin and Tom Bergin NEW YORK, Nov 16 (Reuters) - As winners were being determined on Monday for President Donald Trump's third crypto gala dinn...
articles.body:
NEW YORK, Nov 16 (Reuters) - As winners were being determined on Monday for President Donald Trump's third crypto gala dinner, scheduled for November 22 at his golf club outside Washington, the president's meme coin was trading near 92 cents, a bruising tumble from its high ‌in 2025 of more than $74.

At the peak of Trump's popularity, the token's price surged more than 60% when the first contest was announced in April 2025. Wealthy ‌crypto investors collectively wagered $148 million on what the president promoted as the "most EXCLUSIVE INVITATION in the world." The holdings needed to win a seat at the dinner ranged from $59,000 to $18.5 million.

Today, interest in the third meme coin dinner ​contest has collapsed. It invited 185 holders of the token, known as $TRUMP, to register and see who held the largest amounts during the contest scoring period from September 30 to November 16. The leaderboard at closing showed only 130 crypto wallets — holding a combined $8.6 million — a 94% drop from the first dinner.

The top 29 wallets will be awarded a "Special VIP Reception" with "YOUR FAVORITE PRESIDENT," according to the contest's website, along with VIP seating at the dinner.

This will be the third time Morten Christensen, a crypto entrepreneur from the Netherlands, has qualified for the dinner, but the first where ‌he will be at the VIP reception with the president. He ⁠came in at 26th on the leaderboard with about $41,000 in time-weighted Trump token holdings.

"You can be in a room with the president of the United States, arguably one of the most powerful people in the world," said Christensen. "So why would I not go if it cost me ⁠almost nothing to go?"

His 23-year-old sister, Gabrielle Felen, is also coming along. She bought about 2,000 Trump tokens. She was disappointed she did not make the top 120 — now, she will not get the gift bag.

The contest's muted results come at a time when the Trump family's other crypto-connected equities and ventures have also deflated to record lows. Together, outside investors in ​the ​five main crypto and crypto-linked projects have lost more than $5 billion, according to Reuters estimates.

Most of those losses ​came before the midterm elections in which the Democrats dealt a heavy ‌defeat to Trump's Republican Party, a result that sent prices even lower.

Because the price of the Trump token has continued to fall sharply during the holding period in the run-up to the dinner, the winners have lost millions of dollars in recent weeks.
authors: By Michelle Conlin and Tom Bergin

articles.title: JPMorgan is working on AI agent transactions, and wants to keep humans out of it to make sure ...
articles.summary: America’s biggest bank JPMorgan Chase is exploring a future where artificial intelligence agents will be able to negotiate, agree on terms and also
articles.body: America’s biggest bank JPMorgan Chase is exploring a future where artificial intelligence agents will be able to negotiate, agree on terms and also execute payments with one another without direct human intervention, but the banking giant said that strict controls will be required to make sure that the technology tays within predefined limits. According to a report by CNBC, JPMorgan’s blockchain unit Kinexys and South Korea's Hyundai Card have already completed an initial proof-of-concept which tested how AI agents could handle financial transactions autonomously. The pilot also involved a simulated foreign-exchange transaction designed to help Hyundai Card maintain Euro liquidity in its blockchain-based deposit account.AI agents negotiating with each other is the next goal: JPMorganThe report further states that the next phase of the project will focus on testing what happens when multiple AI agents interact directly with a financial ecosystem, instead of simply carrying out predefined instructions. "What happens when agents are negotiating, agreeing directly with each other and then making payments? What does that actually look like?" said Wee Kee Toh, Global Head of Kinexys Insights at JPMorgan. Speaking to CNBC, Toh said the companies are targeting the first half of 2027 for a more advanced phase that explores autonomous agent-to-agent interactions. "That, I would say, is really the biggest part of what we want to get as an expansion of the phase one scope," he said.JPMorgan wants transactions to remain within strict guardrailsWhile the AI agents could eventually handle complex financial operations independently, JPMorgan feels that governance and oversight still remain the biggest challenge. As per Toh, developing the technology itself was not particularly difficult. The greater hurdle was figuring out accountability and managing the risks associated with allowing AI systems to move money without direct human supervision. In order to address these concerns, Kinexys has built a framework that confines AI agents to authorised parameters and automatically rejects transactions that exceed their permissions."You are going to draw a box around the agent. The agent will never be able to do anything out of the box," Toh said. For example, an AI agent authorised to execute transactions worth up to $5 million would be unable to complete any payment above that threshold.The approach is designed to keep humans out of the transaction process while ensuring agents cannot act beyond predetermined rules and controls.First blockchain-based autonomous treasury testTaking about the initial trials, JPMorgan described it as the first private blockchain-based autonomous bank-agent-to-client-agent test for corporate treasury management. The proof-of-concept included a Hyundai Card AI agent starting a foreign-exchange transaction over Kinexys' blockchain infrastructure without direct involvement. JPMorgan has still not announced a commercial deployment of the technology despite successfully completing the pilot.Partnership could expand across Hyundai groupAlong with this, the companies are also working on evaluating, if the collaboration could be extended to other businesses within Hyundai Motor Group. According to Toh, Hyundai Card's links to the wider group were one of the factors that made the company an attractive partner for the project. Hyundai Motor Group currently owns a majority stake in Hyundai Card through Hyundai Motor, Kia and Hyundai Commercial.Growing push into blockchain paymentsThe AI-agent initiative comes as both companies continue investing in blockchain-based financial infrastructure. Earlier this year, Hyundai Card said it completed a proof-of-concept involving a $20,000 USDT stablecoin transfer between Hyundai Motor's US and Mexican subsidiaries, with settlement and verification taking an average of seven minutes.Meanwhile, Kinexys said in August that it had processed more than $4 trillion in transactions since inception, averaging about $7 billion in daily transaction volume. JPMorgan has also been expanding its digital asset offerings, including the rollout of its dollar-denominated deposit token JPMD for institutional clients.For JPMorgan, the long-term vision is not simply using AI to automate payments, but enabling autonomous agents to negotiate and settle transactions with one another while operating inside tightly controlled boundaries designed to prevent unauthorised actions.Your child uses AI every day. But do they understand it? Find out in the TOI AI Masterclass.

articles.title: Crypto Crashes Pile Up as Once-Diehard Fans Chase New Bets
articles.summary: Every week, crypto gives its diehards another reason to quit as prices sink, trading thins and hacks take their toll.
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Every week, crypto gives its diehards another reason to quit as prices sink, trading thins and hacks take their toll.

Bitcoin broke below $57,742 on Friday for the first time since September 2024, heading for its longest weekly losing streak since 2022. ETF investors are cashing out. The crypto market is worth around $2 trillion, about half its peak last year.

A stronger dollar, rising bets on another Federal Reserve rate increase and jitters over the artificial-intelligence trade hit everything from copper to tech shares this week. But the crash in token prices is now more than a year in the making with the record Binance hack adding to the tumult.

From once-solid stablecoins to Bitcoin and altcoins, the retreat reaches across crypto. Trading volumes have dropped off, too.

At a gathering in New York City this week, a group of young professionals pitched friends still hooked on crypto on other ways to spend their time. Collect coins from all 50 states — actual coins. Walk backward through the city. In fact, doomscrolling on X, one pitch went, beats checking the price of Bitcoin.

James Steinberg, who organized the gathering, called the mission "rehome a crypto bro."

"Crypto is leaving the zeitgeist," he said.

Some of crypto's former diehards have already found new homes for their money. They're buying AI stocks on the bet that the technology will make businesses more productive and profitable even after the recent downturn. They're trading election and earnings outcomes on prediction markets, buying tokenized funds or using perpetual futures to bet on stocks and commodities. They haven't quit speculating. They've quit betting on tokens for their own sake.

Ether has plunged more than 60% since last October, and Solana has lost roughly two-thirds of its value.

The retreat is increasingly showing up in investor behavior. Both short- and long-term holders have been throwing in the towel of late. Short-term holders sent more than 700,000 Bitcoin to the five largest exchanges over the month, increasingly doing so at a loss. Just 2.5% of the Bitcoin they transferred on Wednesday had been in profit, down from roughly 60% in mid-October and the third-lowest reading since 2021, according to data from CryptoQuant.

articles.title: Best Samsung AMOLED phones under Rs 25,000 in India: Samsung Galaxy A26, Galaxy M47, Galaxy M36, Galaxy A17, Galaxy F70 and Galaxy M17
articles.summary: Samsung no longer treats an AMOLED panel as a mid-range perk.
articles.body: Samsung no longer treats an AMOLED panel as a mid-range perk. Across its phones under Rs 25,000, AMOLED is now standard, and the gains show up every day: deeper blacks in films and series, more saturated colours in photos, sharper contrast in dark mode, and screens that hold up better under direct sunlight than the LCD panels they replaced.The rest of the hardware has moved up with it. Most phones in this budget now pair the display with Gorilla Glass Victus protection, a 50MP main camera with optical image stabilisation and a battery of 5,000mAh or more, specifications that sat a tier higher only a couple of years ago. Samsung has also carried its long software commitment down to this range, with six years of Android updates promised on most of its recent models.With so much now shared, the decision comes down to the details. Refresh rate separates the 120Hz models near the top of the budget from the 90Hz phones below them, and from there the differences lie in the chip, battery capacity and charging speed, durability ratings and design, across a price span that runs from around Rs 12,500 to just under Rs 25,000.Samsung Galaxy A26, Samsung Galaxy M47, and other best Samsung phones with AMOLED screens under Rs 25,000 in IndiaPhoneDisplayProcessorRear camerasBatteryPriceSamsung Galaxy A266.7-inch, 120Hz AMOLEDExynos 138050MP (OIS) + 8MP + 2MP5,000mAh, 25WRs 24,999Samsung Galaxy M476.7-inch, 120Hz AMOLEDSnapdragon 6 Gen 350MP (OIS) + 5MP + 2MP6,000mAh, 45WRs 24,999Samsung Galaxy M366.7-inch, 120Hz AMOLEDExynos 138050MP (OIS) + 8MP + 2MP5,000mAh, 25WRs 14,999Samsung Galaxy A176.7-inch, 90Hz AMOLEDExynos 133050MP (OIS) + 5MP + 2MP5,000mAh, 25WRs 18,999Samsung Galaxy F706.7-inch, 90Hz AMOLEDExynos 133050MP (OIS) + 5MP + 2MP5,000mAh, 25WRs 19,999Samsung Galaxy M176.7-inch, 90Hz AMOLEDExynos 133050MP (OIS) triple camera5,000mAh, 25WRs 12,499Samsung Galaxy A26Price: Rs 24,999Specifications: Exynos 1380, 120Hz AMOLED display, IP67 ratingThe Galaxy A26 makes the strongest case for spending close to the top of this budget. Its 6.7-inch FHD+ AMOLED panel runs at 120Hz under Gorilla Glass Victus+, and the IP67 rating covers dust, rain and an accidental drop into water, a level of protection rarely offered at this price.The Exynos 1380 is a known quantity. It keeps One UI responsive and holds steady frame rates in popular games at moderate settings. The camera system is led by a 50MP sensor with optical image stabilisation, which matters most in low light and handheld video, supported by an 8MP ultra-wide, a 2MP macro and a 13MP front camera.What gives the A26 its staying power is the software commitment. Samsung promises six years of OS and security updates, and the phone already carries Galaxy AI tools such as Circle to Search and Object Eraser, along with Knox Vault for sensitive data. The 5,000mAh battery charges at 25W, which suits overnight or desk-side charging.Samsung Galaxy M47Price: Rs 24,999Specifications: Snapdragon 6 Gen 3, 120Hz AMOLED display, 6,000mAh batteryThe Galaxy M47 is built for people whose phones rarely leave their hands. Its 6,000mAh battery is the largest here and supports 45W charging, while bypass charging lets the phone draw power straight from the charger during long gaming sessions, which keeps heat and battery wear in check.The Snapdragon 6 Gen 3 is the most recent chip on this list, and the 6.7-inch Super AMOLED display matches the A26 at 120Hz while reaching 1,400 nits at its peak, which helps with navigation and video outdoors. The camera hardware follows a familiar formula: a 50MP main sensor with OIS and 4K recording, a 5MP ultra-wide, a 2MP macro and a 12MP front camera.Where the A26 leans on durability, the M47 leans on endurance. NFC, expandable storage and six years of updates round out the package, making it the better fit for heavy streamers, mobile gamers and anyone who wants to charge once a day and forget about it.Samsung Galaxy M36Price: Rs 14,999Specifications: Exynos 1380, 120Hz AMOLED display, 50MP OIS cameraThe Galaxy M36 is the most notable value on this list. It brings a 120Hz Super AMOLED display, protected by Gorilla Glass Victus+, to a price well below the two phones above it, and Vision Booster adjusts colour and contrast so the screen stays legible in direct sunlight.It shares the A26's Exynos 1380, with a vapour chamber to keep performance steady over longer sessions, and its 50MP main camera with OIS records 4K video. An 8MP ultra-wide and a 2MP macro complete the rear setup, with a 13MP camera on the front.The 5,000mAh battery charges at 25W, storage can be expanded with a microSD card, and Samsung promises six generations of Android upgrades. For buyers who care most about a smooth, vivid screen and dependable performance, the M36 delivers both while leaving a considerable part of the budget unspent.Samsung Galaxy A17Price: Rs 18,999Specifications: Exynos 1330, 90Hz AMOLED display, IP54 ratingThe Galaxy A17 moves into the 90Hz tier, though its 6.7-inch FHD+ Super AMOLED panel still reaches 1,100 nits and carries Gorilla Glass Victus. In everyday scrolling the step down from 120Hz is gentle, and the panel's contrast and colour remain its strongest qualities.The Exynos 1330 is sized for the essentials: messaging, streaming, social media and casual games. The 50MP main camera with optical image stabilisation, which Samsung calls No Shake Cam, is the one to rely on, with a 5MP ultra-wide, a 2MP macro and a 13MP front camera alongside.The A17's appeal lies in its long-term support and practical extras. Samsung promises six generations of Android upgrades, the IP54 rating covers dust and splashes, storage expands up to 2TB, and a charger comes in the box. On-Device Voice Mail and Circle to Search add everyday convenience to a phone that is meant to last.Samsung Galaxy F70Price: Rs 19,999Specifications: Exynos 1330, 90Hz AMOLED display, 7.5mm bodyThe Galaxy F70 is the newest phone here, and its design is its clearest distinction. At 7.5mm and 192g, it is among the slimmest options in this budget, and its 6.7-inch FHD+ Super AMOLED display runs at 90Hz under Gorilla Glass Victus.Internally, it closely mirrors the A17, with the same Exynos 1330 and a 50MP main camera with optical image stabilisation, joined by a 5MP ultra-wide, a 2MP macro and a 13MP selfie camera. The choice between the two largely comes down to design and price.The 5,000mAh battery charges at 25W, storage expands up to 2TB through a hybrid slot, and NFC is included for payments. Google Gemini, Circle to Search, Samsung Wallet and Knox are built in, which makes it a well-rounded option for buyers who value a thin, light phone with an AMOLED screen under Rs 20,000.Samsung Galaxy M17Price: Rs 12,499Specifications: Exynos 1330, 90Hz AMOLED display, 50MP OIS cameraThe Galaxy M17 shows how far down Samsung's range AMOLED now reaches. At around Rs 12,500, it offers a 6.7-inch FHD+ Super AMOLED panel at 90Hz with a 1,100-nit peak and Gorilla Glass Victus, specifications that belonged to pricier phones only a few years ago.It runs on the same Exynos 1330 as the A17 and F70 and uses a 50MP main camera with optical image stabilisation, alongside a 13MP front camera. The IP54 rating covers dust and splashes.Six years of OS and security updates is the most significant detail at this price, since it extends the useful life of an entry-level phone well beyond what buyers usually expect. Knox Vault and Samsung Wallet with Tap and Pay are included, and the 5,000mAh battery charges at 25W. For first-time smartphone buyers and students, it is a sensible and lasting choice.Fearless legend or grounded realist? articles.title: Too big to ignore. The attacks on Sarvam are a compliment
articles.summary: Something has been building around Sarvam over the past fortnight. A set of posts, most of them about the company's new Token Factory.
articles.body: Something has been building around Sarvam over the past fortnight. A set of posts, most of them about the company's new Token Factory. Anyone can see what they are about. They are not an argument, but almost a narrative whose effect, if not its intent, is to discredit a company that has delivered more for Indian AI than most.So let's see what Sarvam has actually done. It has opened a service called Token Factory. Anyone can now run an AI model for inference on Sarvam controlled GPUs in India, and pay for it in rupees. Eight models are on offer. One is Sarvam's own. Six were built in China. One is Google's. That is the whole of the arrangement, and it is public.The allegation follows from that list. That a company chosen to build India's own AI is now mostly serving foreign models. That it is doing so on government GPUs meant to help Indian innovation, and is therefore giving a fillip to overseas models at Indian expense. That it is, in short, hardly sovereign at all.Now let us understand why this narrative is motivated. For years, the assumption was that AI in the biggest markets would be served by a handful of companies sitting far away. India, with a billion users waiting, was the prize. That assumption has been disturbed by a young Indian company that keeps delivering more than people expected, at prices they cannot match. Those who thought they had a toehold here have been thwarted. Companies thwarted in a market this large do not usually concede. They push back. And the cheapest way to push back is not with a better product. It is with a word like sovereign.It is, therefore, an appeal to sentiment, not to facts. And it sounds patriotic enough that people, high on sentiments, stop checking facts. What follows is genuine confusion about what such a service does. And that confusion is misused to deliberately misinterpret and malign, with a motive that is anything but to tell the truthOne thing is usually left out of these posts. Sarvam's own model was built here, trained here, on data handled here. Sovereignty is not answered by counting how many foreign models sit beside it. It is answered by where the model was trained, where the data sits, and whose laws apply.Let's see what Sarvam is doing.The machines have been bought by Sarvam itself.Access to the government computers that were given for training its own models ended in March 2026.The models it runs are free for anyone to use. Nothing is paid to the companies that built them and no customer data is shared with them.And how many Customer queries sent to a server abroad? None.The machines are in India. The bill is in rupees. None of this is hidden.Now the question. Is it a betrayal of the idea of sovereign AI to run models that were built elsewhere? Let us understand what Sovereignty in practice means. It means the model may have been built anywhere, the machines, the data and the law stay here.Which is why one line from the criticism deserves a second reading. "India's sovereign AI lab is mostly serving Chinese models from Indian GPUs. That's a hosting business, and plenty of companies already run one."Yes. It is a hosting business. That is what such a service is, in California as much as in Chennai or Pune or Bengaluru. The difference is location, currency and law. Plenty of companies run one; very few run one in India. That is the entire point.Then there is the speed comparison, put out by an engineer at a rival company: his company's service, on three of the models, is as fast or faster, and cheaper. It may even be true. But a rival testing himself against a competitor is not an audit. It is a spreadsheet with an interest. And being quicker on three models is not a verdict on a company, a team, or one that built its own model from scratch.Which brings me to what I actually want to say.Sarvam has made the world sit up and notice. Naturally, it is under attack from the powerful competitors. Powerful competitors do not attack a company they expect to fail.Sarvam’s response has to be the only one that has ever worked. Keep delivering. Publish the test results. Let others try the models.And one more thing, offered as advice, perhaps even a complaint. If vested interests are going to keep at this because the stakes have grown, Sarvam cannot answer the same charge from scratch every fortnight. It needs an agile communication strategy that counters with facts, before the noise begins to hurt.The record is already there. It just needs to be told better than it is being denied.Disclaimer: Views expressed above are the author's own.

articles.title: Strategy’s Saylor Stumbles as Firm’s Value Trails Bitcoin Hoard
articles.summary: Strategy Inc.’s Michael Saylor continues to stumble in a year that has put the fundamental principles behind Bitcoin’s largest corporate buyer to the test.
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Strategy Inc.'s Michael Saylor continues to stumble in a year that has put the fundamental principles behind Bitcoin's largest corporate buyer to the test.

While the price of Bitcoin plunged last week, the overall value of the software-maker-turned-cryptocurrency-accumulator dropped back below that of its token holdings. The ratio of its enterprise value — including debt and preferred stock, which Saylor calls mNAV — first breached that threshold in June, raising further questions about the company's funding model.

"The market is quite clearly showing that it has very little interest in leveraged Bitcoin exposure at the moment," said Stéphane Ouellette, founder and chief executive officer of FRNT Financial.

Strategy's enterprise value is around $47 billion, while its 851,305 Bitcoin is worth around $52 billion. Bitcoin dropped to a more than two-year low last week.

On Monday, Strategy increased the amount of its buyback of preferred shares by $1 billion to $4 billion. Saylor — the co-founder and executive chairman — said the firm also repurchased $212 million of its flagship STRC preferred and acquired $29.6 million of Bitcoin from Nov. 16 through Nov. 22.

The company didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

Strategy's ability to raise capital through repeated stock sales and later, perpetual preferred securities, is what gave Saylor a major advantage in expanding the company's ever-larger Bitcoin reserves. By issuing new shares to finance additional purchases, the company developed a self-reinforcing cycle that continuously supported its accumulation strategy.

However, an mNAV of less than 1.0 changes the equation — raising questions about whether Strategy's financing model itself can keep working if the company's securities no longer command a premium, its preferred shares trade at steep discounts and its cost of capital continues to rise.

This year has been marked by attempts by Saylor to revive Strategy's sputtering fundraising machine, which, at one point, was acquiring more Bitcoin than the amount of new Bitcoin created through mining, and was accounting for the majority of net corporate and ETF-related accumulation earlier in 2026. Earlier this month, Strategy started to make daily payments on its preferred shares. Meanwhile, in June, Strategy announced it sold $2.5 million of Bitcoin, the first sale by the firm since 2022.
